paragraphs.text: For the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that was a householder, who went out early in the morning to hire laborers into his vineyard.
paragraphs.original: Ὁμοία γάρ ἐστιν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀνθρώπῳ οἰκοδεσπότῃ ὅστις ἐξῆλθεν ἅμα πρωῒ μισθώσασθαι ἐργάτας εἰς τὸν ἀμπελῶνα αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: Homoia gar estin hē basileia tōn ouranōn anthrōpō oikodespotē hostis exēlthen hama prōi misthōsasthai ergatas eis ton ampelōna autou.

paragraphs.text: And when he had agreed with the laborers for a shilling a day, he sent them into his vineyard.
paragraphs.original: συμφωνήσας δὲ μετὰ τῶν ἐργατῶν ἐκ δηναρίου τὴν ἡμέραν ἀπέστειλεν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸν ἀμπελῶνα αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: symphōnēsas de meta tōn ergatōn ek dēnariou tēn hēmeran apesteilen autous eis ton ampelōna autou.

paragraphs.text: And he went out about the third hour, and saw others standing in the marketplace idle;
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐξελθὼν περὶ τρίτην ὥραν εἶδεν ἄλλους ἑστῶτας ἐν τῇ ἀγορᾷ ἀργούς·
paragraphs.translit: kai exelthōn peri tritēn hōran eiden allous hestōtas en tē agora argous·

paragraphs.text: and to them he said, Go ye also into the vineyard, and whatsoever is right I will give you. And they went their way.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐκείνοις εἶπεν· Ὑπάγετε καὶ ὑμεῖς εἰς τὸν ἀμπελῶνα, καὶ ὃ ἐὰν ᾖ δίκαιον δώσω ὑμῖν·
paragraphs.translit: kai ekeinois eipen· Hypagete kai hymeis eis ton ampelōna, kai ho ean ē dikaion dōsō hymin·

paragraphs.text: Again he went out about the sixth and the ninth hour, and did likewise.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ ἀπῆλθον. πάλιν ἐξελθὼν περὶ ἕκτην καὶ ἐνάτην ὥραν ἐποίησεν ὡσαύτως.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de apēlthon. palin exelthōn peri hektēn kai enatēn hōran epoiēsen hōsautōs.

paragraphs.text: And about the eleventh [hour] he went out, and found others standing; and he saith unto them, Why stand ye here all the day idle?
paragraphs.original: περὶ δὲ τὴν ἑνδεκάτην ἐξελθὼν εὗρεν ἄλλους ἑστῶτας, καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Τί ὧδε ἑστήκατε ὅλην τὴν ἡμέραν ἀργοί;
paragraphs.translit: peri de tēn hendekatēn exelthōn heuren allous hestōtas, kai legei autois· Ti hōde hestēkate holēn tēn hēmeran argoi;

paragraphs.text: They say unto him, Because no man hath hired us. He saith unto them, Go ye also into the vineyard.
paragraphs.original: λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Ὅτι οὐδεὶς ἡμᾶς ἐμισθώσατο. λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ὑπάγετε καὶ ὑμεῖς εἰς τὸν ἀμπελῶνα.
paragraphs.translit: legousin autō· Hoti oudeis hēmas emisthōsato. legei autois· Hypagete kai hymeis eis ton ampelōna.

paragraphs.text: And when even was come, the lord of the vineyard saith unto his steward, Call the laborers, and pay them their hire, beginning from the last unto the first.
paragraphs.original: ὀψίας δὲ γενομένης λέγει ὁ κύριος τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος τῷ ἐπιτρόπῳ αὐτοῦ· Κάλεσον τοὺς ἐργάτας καὶ ἀπόδος αὐτοῖς τὸν μισθὸν ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ τῶν ἐσχάτων ἕως τῶν πρώτων.
paragraphs.translit: opsias de genomenēs legei ho kyrios tou ampelōnos tō epitropō autou· Kaleson tous ergatas kai apodos autois ton misthon arxamenos apo tōn eschatōn heōs tōn prōtōn.

paragraphs.text: And when they came that [were hired] about the eleventh hour, they received every man a shilling.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐλθόντες οἱ περὶ τὴν ἑνδεκάτην ὥραν ἔλαβον ἀνὰ δηνάριον.
paragraphs.translit: kai elthontes hoi peri tēn hendekatēn hōran elabon ana dēnarion.

paragraphs.text: And when the first came, they supposed that they would receive more; and they likewise received every man a shilling.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐλθόντες οἱ πρῶτοι ἐνόμισαν ὅτι πλεῖον λήμψονται· καὶ ἔλαβον τὸ ἀνὰ δηνάριον καὶ αὐτοί.
paragraphs.translit: kai elthontes hoi prōtoi enomisan hoti pleion lēmpsontai· kai elabon to ana dēnarion kai autoi.

paragraphs.text: And when they received it, they murmured against the householder,
paragraphs.original: λαβόντες δὲ ἐγόγγυζον κατὰ τοῦ οἰκοδεσπότου
paragraphs.translit: labontes de egongyzon kata tou oikodespotou

paragraphs.text: saying, These last have spent [but] one hour, and thou hast made them equal unto us, who have borne the burden of the day and the scorching heat.
paragraphs.original: λέγοντες· Οὗτοι οἱ ἔσχατοι μίαν ὥραν ἐποίησαν, καὶ ἴσους αὐτοὺς ἡμῖν ἐποίησας τοῖς βαστάσασι τὸ βάρος τῆς ἡμέρας καὶ τὸν καύσωνα.
paragraphs.translit: legontes· Houtoi hoi eschatoi mian hōran epoiēsan, kai isous autous hēmin epoiēsas tois bastasasi to baros tēs hēmeras kai ton kausōna.

paragraphs.text: But he answered and said to one of them, Friend, I do thee no wrong: didst not thou agree with me for a shilling?
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς ἑνὶ αὐτῶν εἶπεν· Ἑταῖρε, οὐκ ἀδικῶ σε· οὐχὶ δηναρίου συνεφώνησάς μοι;
paragraphs.translit: ho de apokritheis heni autōn eipen· Hetaire, ouk adikō se· ouchi dēnariou synephōnēsas moi;

paragraphs.text: Take up that which is thine, and go thy way; it is my will to give unto this last, even as unto thee.
paragraphs.original: ἆρον τὸ σὸν καὶ ὕπαγε· θέλω δὲ τούτῳ τῷ ἐσχάτῳ δοῦναι ὡς καὶ σοί·
paragraphs.translit: aron to son kai hypage· thelō de toutō tō eschatō dounai hōs kai soi·

paragraphs.text: Is it not lawful for me to do what I will with mine own? or is thine eye evil, because I am good?
paragraphs.original: οὐκ ἔξεστίν μοι ὃ θέλω ποιῆσαι ἐν τοῖς ἐμοῖς; ἢ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου πονηρός ἐστιν ὅτι ἐγὼ ἀγαθός εἰμι;
paragraphs.translit: ouk exestin moi ho thelō poiēsai en tois emois; ē ho ophthalmos sou ponēros estin hoti egō agathos eimi;

paragraphs.text: So the last shall be first, and the first last.
paragraphs.original: οὕτως ἔσονται οἱ ἔσχατοι πρῶτοι καὶ οἱ πρῶτοι ἔσχατοι.
paragraphs.translit: houtōs esontai hoi eschatoi prōtoi kai hoi prōtoi eschatoi.

paragraphs.text: And as Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, he took the twelve disciples apart, and on the way he said unto them,
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἀναβαίνων ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα παρέλαβεν τοὺς δώδεκα μαθητὰς κατʼ ἰδίαν, καὶ ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς·
paragraphs.translit: Kai anabainōn ho Iēsous eis Hierosolyma parelaben tous dōdeka mathētas katʼ idian, kai en tē hodō eipen autois·

paragraphs.text: Behold, we go up to Jerusalem; and the Son of man shall be delivered unto the chief priests and scribes; and they shall condemn him to death,
paragraphs.original: Ἰδοὺ ἀναβαίνομεν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα, καὶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδοθήσεται τοῖς ἀρχιερεῦσιν καὶ γραμματεῦσιν, καὶ κατακρινοῦσιν αὐτὸν θανάτῳ,
paragraphs.translit: Idou anabainomen eis Hierosolyma, kai ho hyios tou anthrōpou paradothēsetai tois archiereusin kai grammateusin, kai katakrinousin auton thanatō,

paragraphs.text: and shall deliver him unto the Gentiles to mock, and to scourge, and to crucify: and the third day he shall be raised up.
paragraphs.original: καὶ παραδώσουσιν αὐτὸν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν εἰς τὸ ἐμπαῖξαι καὶ μαστιγῶσαι καὶ σταυρῶσαι, καὶ τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ ἐγερθήσεται.
paragraphs.translit: kai paradōsousin auton tois ethnesin eis to empaixai kai mastigōsai kai staurōsai, kai tē tritē hēmera egerthēsetai.

paragraphs.text: Then came to him the mother of the sons of Zebedee with her sons, worshipping [him], and asking a certain thing of him.
paragraphs.original: Τότε προσῆλθεν αὐτῷ ἡ μήτηρ τῶν υἱῶν Ζεβεδαίου μετὰ τῶν υἱῶν αὐτῆς προσκυνοῦσα καὶ αἰτοῦσά τι παρʼ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: Tote prosēlthen autō hē mētēr tōn hyiōn Zebedaiou meta tōn hyiōn autēs proskynousa kai aitousa ti parʼ autou.

paragraphs.text: And he said unto her, What wouldest thou? She saith unto him, Command that these my two sons may sit, one on thy right hand, and one on thy left hand, in thy kingdom.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῇ· Τί θέλεις; λέγει αὐτῷ· Εἰπὲ ἵνα καθίσωσιν οὗτοι οἱ δύο υἱοί μου εἷς ἐκ δεξιῶν σου καὶ εἷς ἐξ εὐωνύμων σου ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ σου.
paragraphs.translit: ho de eipen autē· Ti theleis; legei autō· Eipe hina kathisōsin houtoi hoi dyo hyioi mou heis ek dexiōn sou kai heis ex euōnymōn sou en tē basileia sou.

paragraphs.text: But Jesus answered and said, Ye know not what ye ask. Are ye able to drink the cup that I am about to drink? They say unto him, We are able.
paragraphs.original: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Οὐκ οἴδατε τί αἰτεῖσθε· δύνασθε πιεῖν τὸ ποτήριον ὃ ἐγὼ μέλλω πίνειν; λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Δυνάμεθα.
paragraphs.translit: apokritheis de ho Iēsous eipen· Ouk oidate ti aiteisthe· dynasthe piein to potērion ho egō mellō pinein; legousin autō· Dynametha.

paragraphs.text: He saith unto them, My cup indeed ye shall drink: but to sit on my right hand, and on [my] left hand, is not mine to give; but [it is for them] for whom it hath been prepared of my Father.
paragraphs.original: λέγει αὐτοῖς· Τὸ μὲν ποτήριόν μου πίεσθε, τὸ δὲ καθίσαι ἐκ δεξιῶν μου καὶ ἐξ εὐωνύμων οὐκ ἔστιν ἐμὸν δοῦναι, ἀλλʼ οἷς ἡτοίμασται ὑπὸ τοῦ πατρός μου.
paragraphs.translit: legei autois· To men potērion mou piesthe, to de kathisai ek dexiōn mou kai ex euōnymōn ouk estin emon dounai, allʼ hois hētoimastai hypo tou patros mou.

paragraphs.text: And when the ten heard it, they were moved with indignation concerning the two brethren.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ δέκα ἠγανάκτησαν περὶ τῶν δύο ἀδελφῶν.
paragraphs.translit: Kai akousantes hoi deka ēganaktēsan peri tōn dyo adelphōn.

paragraphs.text: But Jesus called them unto him, and said, Ye know that the rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their great ones exercise authority over them.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς προσκαλεσάμενος αὐτοὺς εἶπεν· Οἴδατε ὅτι οἱ ἄρχοντες τῶν ἐθνῶν κατακυριεύουσιν αὐτῶν καὶ οἱ μεγάλοι κατεξουσιάζουσιν αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: ho de Iēsous proskalesamenos autous eipen· Oidate hoti hoi archontes tōn ethnōn katakyrieuousin autōn kai hoi megaloi katexousiazousin autōn.

paragraphs.text: Not so shall it be among you: but whosoever would become great among you shall be your minister;
paragraphs.original: οὐχ οὕτως ἔσται ἐν ὑμῖν· ἀλλʼ ὃς ἂν θέλῃ ἐν ὑμῖν μέγας γενέσθαι ἔσται ὑμῶν διάκονος,
paragraphs.translit: ouch houtōs estai en hymin· allʼ hos an thelē en hymin megas genesthai estai hymōn diakonos,

paragraphs.text: and whosoever would be first among you shall be your servant:
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὃς ἂν θέλῃ ἐν ὑμῖν εἶναι πρῶτος ἔσται ὑμῶν δοῦλος·
paragraphs.translit: kai hos an thelē en hymin einai prōtos estai hymōn doulos·

paragraphs.text: even as the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many.
paragraphs.original: ὥσπερ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου οὐκ ἦλθεν διακονηθῆναι ἀλλὰ διακονῆσαι καὶ δοῦναι τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ λύτρον ἀντὶ πολλῶν.
paragraphs.translit: hōsper ho hyios tou anthrōpou ouk ēlthen diakonēthēnai alla diakonēsai kai dounai tēn psychēn autou lytron anti pollōn.

paragraphs.text: And as they went out from Jericho, a great multitude followed him.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἐκπορευομένων αὐτῶν ἀπὸ Ἰεριχὼ ἠκολούθησεν αὐτῷ ὄχλος πολύς.
paragraphs.translit: Kai ekporeuomenōn autōn apo Ierichō ēkolouthēsen autō ochlos polys.

paragraphs.text: And behold, two blind men sitting by the way side, when they heard that Jesus was passing by, cried out, saying, Lord, have mercy on us, thou son of David.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ δύο τυφλοὶ καθήμενοι παρὰ τὴν ὁδόν, ἀκούσαντες ὅτι Ἰησοῦς παράγει, ἔκραξαν λέγοντες· Κύριε, ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς, υἱὸς Δαυίδ.
paragraphs.translit: kai idou dyo typhloi kathēmenoi para tēn hodon, akousantes hoti Iēsous paragei, ekraxan legontes· Kyrie, eleēson hēmas, hyios Dauid.

paragraphs.text: And the multitude rebuked them, that they should hold their peace: but they cried out the more, saying, Lord, have mercy on us, thou son of David.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ὄχλος ἐπετίμησεν αὐτοῖς ἵνα σιωπήσωσιν· οἱ δὲ μεῖζον ἔκραξαν λέγοντες· Κύριε, ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς, υἱὸς Δαυίδ.
paragraphs.translit: ho de ochlos epetimēsen autois hina siōpēsōsin· hoi de meizon ekraxan legontes· Kyrie, eleēson hēmas, hyios Dauid.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus stood still, and called them, and said, What will ye that I should do unto you?
paragraphs.original: καὶ στὰς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐφώνησεν αὐτοὺς καὶ εἶπεν· Τί θέλετε ποιήσω ὑμῖν;
paragraphs.translit: kai stas ho Iēsous ephōnēsen autous kai eipen· Ti thelete poiēsō hymin;

paragraphs.text: They say unto him, Lord, that our eyes may be opened.
paragraphs.original: λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Κύριε, ἵνα ἀνοιγῶσιν οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ ἡμῶν.
paragraphs.translit: legousin autō· Kyrie, hina anoigōsin hoi ophthalmoi hēmōn.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus, being moved with compassion, touched their eyes; and straightway they received their sight, and followed him.
paragraphs.original: σπλαγχνισθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἥψατο τῶν ὀμμάτων αὐτῶν, καὶ εὐθέως ἀνέβλεψαν καὶ ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: splanchnistheis de ho Iēsous hēpsato tōn ommatōn autōn, kai eutheōs aneblepsan kai ēkolouthēsan autō.
